articles.title: She had trouble paying the rent and built herself a 15-square-meter tiny house on wheels for $30,000: she travels across the United States spending $700 on gas
articles.standfirst: Jenna K. spends a year creating her own home on wheels
articles.summary: Jenna K. spends a year creating her own home on wheels
articles.body:
There are decisions in a person’s life that are important, since they shape the future and how they will devote the rest of their days. Jenna K , in an interview for People magazine, revealed how she decided to leave her job and change course because she was having serious trouble paying the rent . For that reason, she chose to make a 180-degree turn and build her own 15-square-meter tiny house .

The young woman admits that, although she couldn’t say she was short of money, she does regret that she was never able to save because of rent payments. “So I hoped to have a house someday , but that became less and less likely. It seemed that wasn’t going to happen for a very long time,” she says.

Given this situation, Jenna K. explains that one day, after reading an article about tiny houses, she chose to follow that path: “ I built the tiny house in a relative’s backyard and then decided to leave my job and travel with it, since it was a tiny house on wheels, and make documentaries about my travels for a year”.

Trained in film, she quit her job and set off to travel the road after spending $30,000 to shape her 15-square-meter home, which weighs about 4,500 kilograms and has electricity, water, and a plumbing system. She admits that her biggest expense is gasoline , although she ended up staying for a year and a half at a campground, where she only paid for Wi-Fi while working as a host. Now, she has her online channel ‘Tiny Home Giant Journey’ and manages the social media for a tiny house company .

“My main job simply consisted of creating content for my channel and helping it grow. And it wasn’t until years later that it could fully support me without the need for a second job ,” she emphasizes.

articles.title: Ronald Reagan, 40th U.S. President: "You prove that hard work and determination overcome all obstacles and that despair is unnecessary"
articles.standfirst: The former US president believed perseverance and self-confidence could help individuals confront adversity
articles.summary: The former US president believed perseverance and self-confidence could help individuals confront adversity
articles.body:
Success rarely comes without setbacks, and some of life's most meaningful achievements emerge from periods of uncertainty and disappointment. Ronald Reagan , the 40th president of the United States, captured that relationship between adversity and perseverance in a powerful reflection on human determination.

“You prove that hard work and determination overcome all obstacles and that despair is unnecessary,” Reagan said, expressing a belief in the ability of individuals to confront difficult circumstances without surrendering their ambitions.

The message remains relevant far beyond the political environment in which Reagan built his public reputation. It speaks to anyone facing professional setbacks, personal difficulties or uncertainty about the future, emphasizing the importance of continuing to work toward a meaningful objective.

Reagan 's words also reflect the optimism that became a recognizable characteristic of his political identity throughout his presidency, which lasted from 1981 to 1989.

The story behind Ronald Reagan's comments

Reagan delivered the comment on October 4, 1988, during the presentation ceremony for the Minority Enterprise Development Week Awards , where he recognized the achievements of minority business owners across the United States.

His speech addressed the difficulties facing Americans living in disadvantaged communities, particularly those whose experiences had gradually diminished their confidence in the possibility of a better future.

Reagan argued that successful entrepreneurs could inspire others by demonstrating what was achievable through perseverance, self-confidence and access to economic opportunities.

“What is necessary is self-esteem and self-confidence,” Reagan told his audience.

The president viewed meaningful employment and professional achievement as sources of dignity, believing that individual success could have a positive influence extending beyond the person directly responsible for it.

His message was particularly significant because it acknowledged how repeated disappointment could gradually develop into despair, discouraging individuals from pursuing opportunities that might improve their circumstances.

Why Reagan's message remains relevant today

Nearly four decades later, Reagan 's observation continues to resonate in a society where economic uncertainty, professional competition and personal challenges can make long-term ambitions appear increasingly difficult to achieve.

Hard work doesn't necessarily guarantee success, and many obstacles require additional resources, institutional support or assistance from others. Nevertheless, determination can help individuals identify alternative opportunities when their original plans encounter difficulties.

The quote also highlights the importance of recognizing that temporary setbacks do not necessarily define a person's future. Failure can provide valuable experience, while perseverance can create opportunities that initially appeared beyond reach.

Reagan 's underlying message is ultimately about maintaining hope without ignoring the realities of adversity. His words encourage people to recognize their potential, remain adaptable and continue pursuing meaningful goals even when progress appears uncertain.

articles.title: US tourist dies after tragic altercation with former MMA fighter at Bangkok hotel
articles.standfirst: What began as a complaint about excessive noise ended in tragedy
articles.summary: What began as a complaint about excessive noise ended in tragedy
articles.body:
A fatal confrontation between two foreign visitors at a Bangkok hotel has raised questions about the boundaries of self-defense after an American tourist died following an altercation with a former professional mixed martial arts fighter.

Kalif Edward Harper , a 46-year-old from Michigan, was pronounced dead on Sunday, November 22, after emergency responders were unable to revive him following an incident at the Tim Place Hotel in Bangkok's Phra Khanong area.

Thai police subsequently detained Frank Eric Marques , a 39-year-old Italian-Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu black belt and former MMA fighter who reportedly restrained Harper with a chokehold during the confrontation.

Marques remained at the scene and told investigators that he had acted in self-defense. However, authorities are examining whether his response exceeded the force necessary to protect himself.

The incident reportedly began with a disagreement between Harper and hotel employees over excessive noise, with a receptionist later revealing that she had attempted to resolve the complaint before the confrontation occurred.

What happened before fatal confrontation

Receptionist Khang On Nan Kham Bway , 32, told Viral Press that Harper had been complaining about noise from upstairs when Marques entered the hotel's reception area.

“I told him that if he thought it was too loud, he could move to the fifth floor. We hadn’t even finished talking when the Italian man walked in,” Khang recalled.

According to her account, Marques had been passing through the lobby when Harper approached him, prompting a verbal disagreement that subsequently escalated into a physical confrontation.

“They started exchanging words, but I couldn’t understand exactly what they were saying because they were speaking English,” she explained.

Khang also alleged that Harper had threatened her during an earlier complaint, claiming that his behavior had previously made her concerned about her personal safety.

“The American had threatened me once before, saying that if it was still noisy upstairs, he would cut my throat,” she said.

Those allegations remain subject to investigation, with police reviewing surveillance recordings alongside testimony from hotel employees and other available evidence.

Former MMA fighter faces serious legal questions

Marques , known as Frank the Tank within combat sports circles, reportedly holds a professional MMA record of two victories and one defeat, alongside his qualifications in Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu.

According to The Pattaya News, Thai police were proceeding with a murder charge against the Italian despite his assertion that he had acted in self-defense.

Investigators must establish whether the circumstances justified his use of force and whether his actions were proportionate to the threat he allegedly faced.

Harper 's body has been transferred for a forensic examination, with authorities yet to establish a definitive cause of death. Police have also contacted the US Embassy in Bangkok regarding notification of his family.

While preliminary accounts suggest Harper initiated the physical confrontation, responsibility for his death remains a matter for investigators and the judicial process.

Marques has maintained that he was defending himself, and no court has determined his criminal responsibility.

articles.title: Who's performing at the 2026 Macy's Thanksgiving Parade? Complete lineup for this year's celebration
articles.standfirst: The iconic New York celebration marks its 100th edition
articles.summary: The iconic New York celebration marks its 100th edition
articles.body:
A century of Thanksgiving tradition will be celebrated on the streets of New York City on Thursday, November 26, as the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade marks its 100th edition with an extensive entertainment lineup befitting the historic occasion.

Country music sensation Megan Moroney and singer Teddy Swims will headline performances outside Macy's Herald Square flagship store, while artists representing generations and musical genres will entertain spectators along the parade route.

Among the most anticipated moments will be a special tribute to Dolly Parton , led by Broadway performer Megan Hilty . Singer and songwriter EJAE will also deliver a featured performance during the anniversary celebration.

The musical entertainment will accompany a massive collection of floats, marching bands and a record 100 inflatable elements, combining contemporary popular culture with characters that helped establish the parade's enduring appeal.

Performers at 2026 Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade

Macy's has assembled a diverse musical lineup featuring internationally recognized artists, TV personalities and Broadway talent. The announced performers include:

- Jimmy Fallon & The Roots

Several familiar television and entertainment personalities will also make special appearances, including Melissa Joan Hart, Jack McBrayer, Janet McTeer, Holly Robinson Peete and Rodney Peete .

Marching bands from across the United States will provide additional entertainment, including the University of Alabama's Million Dollar Band , the University of Connecticut Marching Band and the University of Illinois Marching Illini .

Performances from the Divine Nine Unity Step Team, Native Pride Productions, Spirit of America Cheer, Spirit of America Dance and the Maria Verdeja School of the Arts will further expand the celebration.

When and where to watch Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade 2026

The Thanksgiving Day festivities begin at 8:30 a.m. on Thursday, November 26, with NBC, Telemundo and Peacock providing coverage until noon in all US time zones.

Savannah Guthrie, Hoda Kotb and Al Roker will lead NBC's broadcast, while Andrea Meza, Aleyda Ortiz and Clovis Nienow will present the Spanish-language coverage on Telemundo.

Spectators attending in person will see the procession begin near West 77th Street and Central Park West before making its way through Manhattan toward Herald Square.

The centennial edition will also welcome back historic balloon characters, including Felix the Cat, Blue Hippopotamus and Underdog , which last appeared in the parade in 1984.

New designs featuring Sorcerer's Apprentice Mickey, Bluey, Hello Kitty and Buckaroo Bob the Minion will join the procession, alongside floats celebrating the event's extensive history.

As tradition dictates, Santa Claus will bring the parade to its conclusion, officially ushering in the Christmas shopping season. NBC will also broadcast an encore presentation at 2 p.m. ET/PT.

articles.title: Mega Millions Winning Numbers: Results for Tuesday, November 24 drawing of the $645 Million Jackpot
articles.standfirst: Tuesday's drawing offers one of the biggest Mega Millions prizes of 2026
articles.summary: Tuesday's drawing offers one of the biggest Mega Millions prizes of 2026
articles.body:
A Thanksgiving week celebration could take on an entirely different meaning for one American lottery player on Tuesday, November 24, as the Mega Millions jackpot reaches an estimated $645 million following another drawing without a grand prize winner.

Friday's unsuccessful jackpot drawing pushed the prize closer to $650 million , with Tuesday's potential winner being offered a choice between the full advertised amount in annual installments or an immediate cash payment of approximately $270.8 million before taxes .

The growing jackpot is among the biggest Mega Millions prizes of 2026, although it remains some distance behind the $803 million won by a Florida ticket holder in July, the largest Mega Millions jackpot awarded this year.

Tuesday's drawing is scheduled for 11 p.m. ET , with official results expected shortly afterward. The winning numbers will determine whether the jackpot has finally been claimed or continues growing ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday weekend.

Mega Millions winning numbers for Tuesday, November 24, 2026

The winning numbers for Tuesday's $645 million Mega Millions jackpot are pending, with the drawing scheduled to take place at 11 p.m. ET.

During the previous drawing on Friday, November 20, the winning white ball numbers were 32, 35, 48, 58 and 61, while the gold Mega Ball was 21. No ticket matched all six numbers.

However, six players successfully matched four white balls and the Mega Ball. Their respective prize multipliers increased their winnings to amounts ranging from $20,000 to $100,000 before taxes.

The odds of winning the Mega Millions jackpot stand at approximately one in 290.5 million, while the lottery offers eight additional prize categories involving different combinations of matching numbers.

How much would the $645 million Mega Millions winner actually take home?

The difference between the advertised jackpot and the eventual payout could be substantial, particularly if the winner follows the popular approach of accepting an immediate lump sum rather than annual installments.

According to Forbes, the estimated $270.8 million cash option would initially be reduced to approximately $205.8 million following the mandatory 24% federal tax withholding.

The winner's eventual federal income tax obligations could reduce that amount further to approximately $170.6 million . Additional state and local taxes may apply depending on where the winning ticket was purchased and the winner's individual circumstances.

Choosing the annuity would provide 30 payments , with each successive annual installment increasing by 5% . Forbes estimates that the total payout after federal taxes could reach approximately $406.3 million over the payment period.

Should Tuesday's drawing produce another rollover, the next opportunity for the jackpot to be claimed will come on Friday, November 27, when Mega Millions holds its regularly scheduled Black Friday drawing.

articles.title: Barnes and Noble Black Friday sale: Best deals, discounts and opening time this Friday
articles.standfirst: Book lovers can already shop early online before brick-and-mortar stores open their doors on November 27
articles.summary: Book lovers can already shop early online before brick-and-mortar stores open their doors on November 27
articles.body:
Bookworms and holiday gift shoppers do not have to wait until the Thanksgiving leftovers are packed away to start crossing titles off their wish lists.

Barnes & Noble has already rolled out its 2026 Black Friday and Cyber Monday event online at BarnesandNoble.com, offering steep markdowns across bestselling fiction, nonfiction, young adult box sets, vinyl records, and boutique gifts through Monday, November 30, 2026.

Still, for readers hoping to browse the aisles in person, or snag coveted in-store exclusives, knowing when local doors unlock on Friday morning is essential.

All Barnes & Noble retail locations across the United States close on Thanksgiving Day, Thursday, November 26, before reopening for Black Friday on Friday, November 27.

Because the bookseller operates both standalone street-level stores and locations inside enclosed shopping malls, exact opening hours vary by neighborhood.

Most standalone Barnes & Noble stores open early on Black Friday, typically at 8:00 a.m. or 9:00 a.m. local time, roughly an hour ahead of standard weekday schedules, while mall-based stores align with their shopping center’s holiday opening time.

Shoppers planning an early morning visit should confirm their nearest branch’s schedule via the online Store Locator, especially since Black Friday morning traditionally marks the in-store debut of Barnes & Noble ’s annual Signed Editions collection, where limited quantities of autographed books sell on a first-come, first-served basis.

Top Black Friday book, collectible, and media deals available right now

articles.summary: Powerball’s grand prize climbed past the $30 million mark to an estimated $31 million annuity ahead of Wednesday’s 10:59 p.m. ET Thanksgiving Eve drawing
articles.body:
Lottery players hoping to kick off the Thanksgiving holiday with a multimillion-dollar windfall have their eyes fixed on tonight’s Powerball drawing.

Scheduled for Wednesday, November 25, 2026, at 10:59 p.m. ET (3:59 a.m. GMT on Thursday, November 26) at the Florida Lottery draw studio in Tallahassee, Florida, tonight’s drawing features an estimated $31 million grand prize, with a lump-sum cash option worth $13 million before federal and state tax withholdings.

Because the live broadcast has not yet taken place, the official winning numbers for Wednesday night remain pending and will be posted immediately once the balls drop.

Tonight’s jackpot climbed above the $30 million threshold after Monday night’s November 23 drawing ended without a top-prize winner.

Following a $114 million jackpot win on Saturday, November 21, the game had reset to its $20 million starting prize for Monday’s drawing, where the winning numbers drawn were 7, 9, 27, 40, and 58, with a red Powerball of 19 and a 2X Power Play multiplier. In Monday’s separate Double Play drawing, the winning numbers were 35, 36, 40, 48, and 51, with a Double Play Powerball of 3.

Although nobody hit the jackpot or matched all five white balls for the $1 million second-tier prize on Monday, more than 283,857 tickets nationwide won cash prizes, including 11 tickets that matched four white balls plus the red Powerball to win $50,000, and two additional Power Play tickets that doubled that payout to $100,000.

How to play Powerball tonight, ticket deadlines, and all nine prize tiers

Players looking to enter Wednesday night’s Thanksgiving Eve drawing must purchase their tickets before their local jurisdiction’s cutoff deadline, which typically closes one to two hours prior to the 10:59 p.m. ET broadcast.

Standard Powerball tickets cost $2 per play across 45 U.S. states, Washington, D.C., Puerto Rico, and the U.S. Virgin Islands, as well as in the United Kingdom, where Powerball ticket sales expanded in July 2026, while tickets in Idaho and Montana start at $3 because the Power Play feature is automatically included.

To play, participants pick five white-ball numbers between 1 and 69 and one red Powerball number from 1 to 26, or opt for a computer-generated “Quick Pick.”

For an extra $1 per play, adding Power Play multiplies non-jackpot prizes by 2X, 3X, 4X, 5X, or 10X, with the 10X multiplier active tonight because the advertised jackpot sits below $150 million, and automatically boosts the Match 5 prize to $2 million.

Players in participating jurisdictions can also add Double Play for another $1, entering their numbers into a second drawing with a $10 million top prize.

Across the main Powerball drawing, players can win across nine prize levels with overall odds of 1 in 24.87:

- Match 5 white balls + Powerball: Grand Prize ($31 million estimated annuity) — Odds: 1 in 292,201,338

- Match 5 white balls only: $1,000,000 ($2,000,000 with Power Play) — Odds: 1 in 11,688,053.52

- Match 4 white balls + Powerball: $50,000 — Odds: 1 in 913,129.18

- Match 4 white balls only: $100 — Odds: 1 in 36,525.17

- Match 3 white balls + Powerball: $100 — Odds: 1 in 14,494.11

- Match 3 white balls only: $7 — Odds: 1 in 579.76

- Match 2 white balls + Powerball: $7 — Odds: 1 in 701.33

- Match 1 white ball + Powerball: $4 — Odds: 1 in 91.98

- Match red Powerball only: $4 — Odds: 1 in 38.32

Fans can watch tonight’s drawing live on local television stations or stream it directly on Powerball.com . Should a ticket match all six numbers, the winner can choose between a one-time lump sum or an annuity paid out over 30 graduated installments across 29 years.

articles.title: A Florida man bought an abandoned town in California for $1.4 million: Eight years later, here's how his life has changed
articles.standfirst: Eight years after risking his life savings on a forgotten mining town, he's still determined to bring it back to life
articles.summary: Eight years after risking his life savings on a forgotten mining town, he's still determined to bring it back to life
articles.body:
What started as an unexpected property listing has completely transformed Brent Underwood's life. In 2018, the Florida -born entrepreneur took an extraordinary financial gamble, purchasing Cerro Gordo, an abandoned mining town in California , for $1.4 million.

Eight years later, he's still committed to the remote settlement, having traded the comforts of the city for a life dedicated to rebuilding a piece of American history.

Underwood was living in Austin, Texas, when a friend sent him the listing as something of a joke. Having previously operated a bed-and-breakfast in a Victorian property, he was already interested in historic buildings and hospitality. Cerro Gordo, however, presented an opportunity on a different scale.

More than just one historic property, he could potentially bring an entire forgotten community back to life. Interested in the idea, he researched the settlement, travelled to California and eventually secured the purchase.

The financial commitment was enormous. Underwood didn't have the money to buy the town outright, relying on a high-interest loan, his life savings and contributions from friends.

“The whole project has been a big risk from day one,” he told People. “I pushed all of my savings into this project without a super clear path to make it back.”

He had no professional background in mining or construction either. The risk was considerable, but he saw the challenge as an opportunity to push himself beyond his existing experience.

Eight years later, a risky purchase has become a lifelong mission

The years since the purchase have brought significant changes. Underwood eventually moved to Cerro Gordo full-time, spending six years living in the isolated settlement.

Situated around 8,200 feet above sea level near Death Valley, the town offers little of the convenience associated with modern living. There's no running water or mobile phone coverage, while the nearest grocery store is approximately two hours away.

Winter can be particularly demanding, with heavy snowfall and difficult access sometimes leaving him stranded for days. Even basic tasks require advance planning, and maintaining ageing buildings in such a remote location presents its own challenges.

Nevertheless, restoring properties and uncovering the settlement's past have become central to his everyday life.

One particularly memorable discovery came when he found a briefcase hidden beneath dusty boxes in the old general store. Its contents included mining claims, financial records, love letters and legal documents, revealing the personal story of a former resident who had repeatedly tried to make a living in the mountains.

Underwood says he identified with the miner's determination, recognizing similarities between the man's ambitions and his own uncertain journey.

His restoration efforts have also attracted a substantial online audience. Through TikTok, Instagram and YouTube, he shares discoveries, construction projects and the realities of living in a ghost town. His following has grown into the millions, bringing international attention to Cerro Gordo.

Meanwhile, plans to develop visitor accommodation and restore historic buildings continue, including rebuilding the American Hotel, which was destroyed by fire in 2020.

Although the financial pressures haven't disappeared and the original investment remains a significant commitment, Underwood believes the experience has been worth it.

articles.title: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade suspended: why will the traditional parade won't take place tomorrow and when will be celebrated?
articles.standfirst: Macy’s Thanksgiving Parade makes history: first-ever postponement in 100 years
articles.summary: Macy’s Thanksgiving Parade makes history: first-ever postponement in 100 years
articles.body:
Macy’s 100th Thanksgiving Day Parade will make history for an unexpected reason: it will not take place on Thanksgiving Day.

Organizers announced an unprecedented decision to postpone the iconic event until Saturday due to severe weather conditions expected to impact New York City .

The parade, originally scheduled for Thursday, was moved “out of an abundance of caution” after discussions with city officials regarding the storm threat, Macy’s said in a statement.

“Our team is now working through the complex operational logistics required to bring the Parade to life on Saturday, and we will share additional details as they are finalized,” the company said.

The postponement comes as a powerful storm system is expected to bring strong winds and heavy rain to the region, raising concerns about the safety of the parade’s famous giant balloons as they travel through the streets of Manhattan surrounded by skyscrapers and thousands of spectators.

New York officials prioritize safety

New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani defended the decision, saying the expected winds could be strong enough to break tree branches and damage power lines.

“I know many New Yorkers, myself included, as well as millions around the world, were looking forward to the parade being held tomorrow,” Mamdani said. “But safety has to come first.”

The National Weather Service issued high wind and coastal flood warnings for Thursday and Friday. City officials also took additional precautions, including restrictions on empty tractor-trailers crossing bridges during the storm.

NBC, which traditionally broadcasts the parade, announced it will air a replay of the 2025 edition on Thursday instead.

First postponement in parade history

According to Macy’s, this marks the first time the Thanksgiving Day Parade has been postponed . The event was canceled only three times, in 1942, 1943 and 1944 , due to World War II.

The parade’s balloons have been grounded because of weather only once before, in 1971 .

New York has long maintained safety protocols regarding the famous balloons, including when winds become too dangerous to allow them to fly. Those measures were strengthened after a 1997 incident when strong winds sent a balloon into a metal pole, leaving a spectator seriously injured.

Some performers already confirmed for Saturday

It remains unclear how much of the original lineup will be affected by the schedule change, but several Broadway productions, including “Wicked,” “Hamilton,” “Chicago,” “The Lost Boys,” “The Rocky Horror Show” and “Paddington the Musical,” confirmed their performers will participate on Saturday.

Macy’s executive Will Coss said organizers remain optimistic about delivering the full celebration.

“Everyone understands what we’re up against and is rallying behind us to create the best and most successful 100th parade,” he said.

For some visitors, the delay even brought an unexpected benefit. Sarah Collins and her 12-year-old son had planned a New York trip that did not originally include the parade because they were arriving Friday. After the postponement, they will now be able to attend.

The rescheduled parade will begin at 8:30 a.m. Saturday , according to Macy’s.

articles.title: What time does stores open on Black Friday? This are the opening and closing times for tomorrow
articles.standfirst: Black Friday arrives on Friday, November 27, with major retailers and shopping centers preparing for a busy day of bargain hunting
articles.summary: Black Friday arrives on Friday, November 27, with major retailers and shopping centers preparing for a busy day of bargain hunting
articles.body:
Black Friday is the unofficial kickoff to the United States ’ holiday shopping season, falling each year on the day after Thanksgiving as retailers use the date to advertise discounts on electronics, clothing, toys and home goods, while shoppers look for deals ahead of Christmas . The event is now much bigger than a single day of sales as promotions often begin weeks earlier and continue through the weekend into Cyber Monday , blending in-store doorbusters with online offers – but, even so, Black Friday remains a major moment for retailers hoping to turn holiday interest into spending.

Its name, however, did not begin as a celebration of bargain hunting as the phrase is widely traced to Philadelphia in the 1950s and early 1960s, when police used it to jest in description of the traffic jams and crowds that overwhelmed the city on the Friday after Thanksgiving . Shoppers and visitors were pouring into Philadelphia ahead of the Army-Navy football game, whilst downtown stores were packed as the Christmas shopping season got underway meaning police faced long shifts managing congestion and busy sidewalks, giving the day a reputation that merchants initially found unhelpful. But retailers later helped give the name a more positive meaning by linking it to the accounting idea of moving from “the red” into “the black” as sales improved and that triggered a marketing-friendly reinvention rather than the phrase's original, and less enthusiastic, source.

What time do stores open on Black Friday 2026?

Black Friday spread nationally as retailers expanded promotions and shoppers came to expect steep discounts on sought-after products as early openings, limited-stock doorbusters and newspaper ads made the day an annual event that celebrates low prices. The day gives consumers a chance to compare competing offers and tackle holiday gift lists, whilst stores gain a high-profile opportunity to attract new, life-long, customers. Online shopping has widened the audience, but opening-day deals still draw people into stores. This year, Black Friday falls on Friday, November 27 and plenty of stores are opening early on as Kohl’s and JCPenney have scheduled stores to open at 5am local time, as wil l Academy Sports + Outdoors , Bass Pro Shops and Cabella’s . Walmart , Target and Home Depot are scheduled to open at 6am local time, alongside Best Buy , Lowe’s , Macy’s and Dick’s Sporting Goods . Best Buy and Macy’s list 10pm closings, while Walmart expects most stores to close at 11pm local time nationwide. Other retailers are taking a later start as T.J. Maxx and Marshalls are listed for 7am, and Hobby Lobby is scheduled to open at 8am. Costco warehouses generally open at 9am for executive members and 10am for other members, offering an exclusive jump on the discounts.

articles.title: Are banks closed the day after Thanksgiving? Here are the hours they will be open during the holidays
articles.standfirst: Most banks will close for Thanksgiving before reopening on Black Friday, but customers should be aware of regional exceptions
articles.summary: Most banks will close for Thanksgiving before reopening on Black Friday, but customers should be aware of regional exceptions
articles.body:
Thanksgiving is one of the few days of the year when much of the United States ’ banking system shuts its doors, leaving customers to rely on ATMs and digital services, but the pause is brief as most bank branches are expected to swiftly reopen on Friday, November 27. Although Black Friday is technically not a federal banking holiday, it is still one of the busiest shopping days of the year and a major boost to the US economy – meaning it is treated slightly differently to a standard Friday across the other weeks of the calendar year.

Thanksgiving is on Thursday, November 26 meaning a large number of banks will close for the day, but that does not include the following Friday, meaning banks can resume normal business for anyone planning to visit a branch, deposit a check or speak to a teller. Major institutions including Chase , Bank of America and Wells Fargo are expected to reopen on Friday, although customers should check their local branch because opening and closing times can vary across the United States . City National Bank , for example, says its branches will be open on Friday, with the exception of Nevada offices observing Nevada Family Day as a reminder that regional observances and individual bank decisions can affect a small number of locations. Ensure to check before attending.

What banking services are available during the holidays?

Thanksgiving itself is different as banks generally tend to close their physical branches on in line with the holiday schedule of the Federal Reserve , including some of the branches inside supermarkets or other retail locations - although they may follow special arrangements. Fortunately for those needing to make withdrawals, digital banking services and ATMs generally remain available throughout Thanksgiving and Black Friday as customers can usually check balances, transfer money between eligible accounts, pay bills and deposit checks through a mobile app. Availability can depend on the bank and the type of transaction and it should be remembered that payment processing is separate from account access as because the Federal Reserve ’s payment systems observe Thanksgiving , ACH transfers, direct deposits and payments may not be processed until the next business day. Thus, seeing a transaction in an app does not mean it has cleared. Anyone expecting an important payment or needing cash for the holiday weekend should plan ahead and confirm timing with their bank. Most branches reopen Friday, but Thanksgiving can shift processing schedules, and some regional offices observe other holidays. Check with the institution before making plans.

articles.title: What are the New Laws that will come to effect starting 2027? Employment, tech, and cost adjustment starting in January
articles.standfirst: New state legislation will bring changes to workplace protections, artificial intelligence, online safety and household costs when 2027 begins
articles.summary: New state legislation will bring changes to workplace protections, artificial intelligence, online safety and household costs when 2027 begins
articles.body:
Americans will enter 2027 with a fresh set of laws affecting workplaces across the United States as digital services and household expenses as several changes take effect on January 1 - although the rules are not nationwide as they apply in the states that enacted them. The measures cover a wide range of everyday issues, from how employers monitor staff to the way artificial intelligence is used in important decisions whilst other changes place new responsibilities on app stores and data center operators, while some address costs linked to housing and essential services.

For example, workers in Illinois will receive additional protection when volunteering as emergency responders as House Bill 1353 prevents public and private employers from disciplining or dismissing covered workers for responding to emergencies or attending required training, subject to an exception for municipalities with populations of 7500 or above. Whilst California is also tightening limits on workplace monitoring through Assembly Bill 1331 , which restricts employers from using surveillance tools in bathrooms, locker rooms, changing areas and lactation spaces, addressing concerns about the collection of workers’ personal data in places where privacy is expected. And New York is extending paid family leave eligibility to certain construction employees as the Senate Bill 8795 covers qualifying workers employed for at least 26 of the previous 39 weeks by covered employers that are signatories to collective bargaining agreements.

Technology laws target AI and online safety

Artificial intelligence is another major focus as Colorado Senate Bill 189 introduces requirements for developers and businesses using automated decision-making technology in consequential areas such as employment, housing, lending, insurance and health care, including disclosures and opportunities for human review. Alabama ’s App Store Accountability Act requires app store providers to request and verify users’ age categories, link minor accounts with parent accounts and obtain parental consent for certain downloads and purchases. The law takes effect January 1, 2027. New York is also introducing transparency requirements for developers of frontier AI models, including measures to disclose information and report critical safety incidents as these provisions add to a growing patchwork of state rules governing how powerful AI systems are developed and deployed. Tennessee law requires data center owners or operators to pay for electrical infrastructure needed to serve their facilities, preventing utilities from passing those additional costs on to residential and other business customers as demand grows statewide. California is changing the treatment of certain insurance proceeds held by financial institutions, and under Assembly Bill 1278 , lenders holding hazard-insurance payments in loss-draft accounts for qualifying homes must credit or pay borrowers at least two percent annual simple interest, subject to the law’s conditions.

articles.title: When are you getting your Social Security Payment for December 2026? Schedule for next month's deposit
articles.standfirst: The holiday calendar means certain Americans will receive two deposits next month
articles.summary: The holiday calendar means certain Americans will receive two deposits next month
articles.body:
With Christmas approaching and household expenses increasing during the holiday season, millions of Americans who rely on Social Security benefits will be paying close attention to their bank accounts throughout December. This year's payment calendar contains an important adjustment that will see certain recipients receive two deposits within the same month.

The Social Security Administration (SSA) has scheduled payments across six dates in December 2026, with most retirement, disability and survivor benefit recipients receiving their money according to their date of birth.

However, the timing of New Year's Day and the first weekend of January 2027 means that payments normally scheduled for early January will arrive before the end of December for certain beneficiaries.

The adjustment is particularly significant for Americans receiving Supplemental Security Income (SSI), a federal program that provides financial assistance to qualifying individuals with disabilities, blindness or limited financial resources who meet the program's eligibility requirements.

While receiving two deposits in December may offer some financial flexibility during the holidays, beneficiaries should understand that the second payment is not an additional benefit, Christmas bonus or stimulus check.

Full Social Security payment schedule for December 2026

Most Americans receiving Social Security retirement or Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI) benefits are paid on the second, third or fourth Wednesday of each month, depending on their birthday.

The complete December 2026 payment schedule is as follows:

Tuesday, December 1: Regular December SSI payments.

Thursday, December 3: Payments for beneficiaries who began receiving Social Security before May 1997 and other qualifying recipients.

Wednesday, December 9: Beneficiaries with birthdays between the 1st and 10th of the month.

Wednesday, December 16: Beneficiaries with birthdays between the 11th and 20th of the month.

Wednesday, December 23: Beneficiaries with birthdays between the 21st and 31st of the month.

Thursday, December 31: Early January SSI payments and Social Security deposits for qualifying beneficiaries normally paid on the third of the month.

Americans receiving spousal or survivor benefits generally have their payment dates determined by the birthday of the person whose earnings record establishes their entitlement.

Why some payments will arrive early in December

The SSA doesn't issue scheduled benefit payments on weekends or federal holidays. With January 1 falling on New Year's Day and January 3 falling on a Sunday, affected payments will instead be distributed on December 31.

SSI recipients will also receive their first payment reflecting the 2027 cost-of-living adjustment (COLA), which increases benefits by 3.6%. Regular Social Security benefits will reflect the increase beginning with payments for December benefits, ordinarily distributed in January.

Beneficiaries receiving early deposits should budget accordingly, as their next regularly scheduled payments won't arrive until February .

Anyone experiencing difficulties receiving their money should initially contact their bank or financial institution. Individual payment information is also available through a My Social Security account or by contacting the SSA at 800-772-1213.

articles.title: IShowSpeed takes livestreams to the limit and confirms his next big challenge: traveling to outer space
articles.standfirst: The American content creator assures in LIFE magazine that the project is already underway
articles.summary: The American content creator assures in LIFE magazine that the project is already underway
articles.body:
When it seemed there were no frontiers left to cross in content creation, IShowSpeed has once again left the internet speechless. The popular American streamer (Darren Watkins Jr.) has officially confirmed that his next big project will be to travel to outer space and broadcast it live to millions of viewers.

The announcement came as part of his cover interview for the special relaunch issue of LIFE magazine . Although the 21-year-old creator had already hinted at this ambitious idea in the past, this time he assured that the plan is already a reality in progress: “I can’t say too much about it, but it’s going to happen” , he stated emphatically.

An unprecedented technical challenge in the history of streaming

For the moment, secrecy surrounds the logistical side of the mission. No exact date for the liftoff has been disclosed , nor which private aerospace company will be behind the launch, although all eyes inevitably point to SpaceX , the company whose founder, Elon Musk , the streamer himself has already publicly asked for help on previous occasions.

If it comes to fruition, the project would mark a before and after for digital entertainment , as it would require solving a major technical challenge: ensuring a stable connection in orbit to broadcast without interruptions. Speed already showed his interest in science last year by collaborating with engineers and former astronauts, but leaving the atmosphere would take his extreme challenges to another level.

This space adventure will serve as the crowning touch to his mammoth IRL world tour (in real life), a project with which he has already traveled to nearly a hundred countries with the goal of visiting every nation on the planet before leaving Earth. With this move, the recent three-time consecutive winner of the Streamer of the Year award aims to pull off what would undoubtedly be the most ambitious livestream ever made.

articles.standfirst: The fourth-largest lottery jackpot of 2026 is up for grabs on Black Friday
articles.summary: The fourth-largest lottery jackpot of 2026 is up for grabs on Black Friday
articles.body:
Thanksgiving weekend could deliver a life-changing surprise for a lottery player in the United States after the Mega Millions jackpot climbed to an estimated $673 million following another drawing without a grand prize winner earlier this week.

Friday's drawing on November 27 represents another opportunity for someone to claim what would be the second-largest Mega Millions jackpot of 2026, with the prize continuing to grow after Tuesday's winning combination failed to produce a jackpot winner.

The latest rollover has increased the estimated lump sum cash option to $282.6 million, although the amount an eventual winner receives would depend on their preferred payment method and applicable taxes.

The jackpot is also closing in on the $800 million Mega Millions prize claimed by a Florida ticket holder in July, which remains the lottery's biggest payout of the year.

Mega Millions winning numbers for Friday, November 27, 2026

The latest Mega Millions drawing is scheduled for 11 p.m. ET on Friday, November 27, with the official winning numbers expected to be released shortly afterward.

Friday's winning numbers have still to be drawn.

The winning numbers from the previous Mega Millions drawing on Tuesday, November 24 , were:

White balls: 38, 42, 44, 45, 62.

Players must match all five white balls and the gold Mega Ball to claim the jackpot, although several additional prize categories are available to ticket holders who match fewer numbers.

The odds of securing the Mega Millions grand prize stand at approximately one in 290.4 million, compared with Powerball's jackpot odds of approximately one in 292.2 million.

How much will Mega Millions jackpot winner receive after taxes?

The advertised $673 million jackpot represents the total value of the annuity option, which consists of 30 payments that increase by 5% annually. Winners can alternatively choose to receive a single cash payment of $282.6 million before taxes.

Under the cash option, mandatory federal withholding of 24% would initially reduce the payout to approximately $214.8 million. Applying the highest federal marginal income tax rate of 37% would leave an estimated $178 million before additional state or local taxes.

Someone selecting the annuity could receive approximately $424 million over the payment period, assuming a federal tax rate of 37%, although future tax rates could affect the final amount.

articles.title: “No, Mr. President.” U.S. troops greet Trump with an awkward silence after he offered Melania to take questions about Ukraine
articles.standfirst: Troops decline Trump's invitation to quiz First Lady on Russia-Ukraine ceasefire
articles.summary: Troops decline Trump's invitation to quiz First Lady on Russia-Ukraine ceasefire
articles.body:
Donald Trump faced an awkward moment during his Thanksgiving video call with U.S. troops after inviting them to ask First Lady Melania Trump about her involvement in Russia-Ukraine diplomacy.

The invitation was met with an uncomfortable silence before one soldier politely declined the opportunity on behalf of his fellow service members.

The president spoke from his Mar-a-Lago resort in Florida, connecting with Lieutenant Colonel Juan Rivera and approximately 10 soldiers from the 1st Battalion, 7th Air Defense Artillery Regiment, who were deployed overseas.

Trump praised their military service and made remarks about their continued deployment, suggesting they would remain stationed abroad for as long as he decided.

He also expressed confidence about achieving victory before shifting the conversation toward his wife, who was sitting beside him.

Trump highlighted Melania's involvement in humanitarian efforts connected to the conflict between Russia and Ukraine, suggesting the soldiers could ask her about a temporary ceasefire.

"If you have something to ask — we have our first lady here," Trump said. "She did a ceasefire with Russia-Ukraine."

However, his invitation didn't generate the response he appeared to expect.

Nobody immediately volunteered a question. Trump looked toward the laptop screen, raised an eyebrow and waited as the silence continued. Eventually, Rivera stepped in to answer on behalf of the group.

“No, Mr. President, I don’t think we have any questions right now,” the soldier replied.

Rivera then thanked Trump for taking the time to speak with the troops and extended Thanksgiving wishes to his family. Trump acknowledged the response and quickly moved forward with the conversation.

Ukraine diplomacy faces mounting uncertainty

The uncomfortable exchange came amid growing questions about Washington's approach to the war and the international community's commitment to supporting Kyiv.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy recently criticized Trump's friendly description of Russian President Vladimir Putin following their interaction at a summit in China.

Speaking to the BBC, Zelenskyy described the exchange as strange and insisted Putin shouldn't be regarded as a friend given Russia's invasion of Ukraine.

Zelenskyy also expressed frustration over what he considers insufficient American attention to the conflict, particularly delays involving promised Patriot missile deliveries. He warned that shortages of the crucial air defense systems could cost lives as Russian attacks continue.

Meanwhile, European leaders are struggling to agree on additional financial assistance for Ukraine. A Brussels summit ended without an agreement on the European Union's proposed 2028-2034 budget, leaving a planned €45 billion loan for Kyiv facing further uncertainty.

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz supports including the funding in the bloc's financial plans, but several countries, including Hungary and Slovakia, have raised objections.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen acknowledged that discussions had made progress but stressed that considerable negotiations remained before an agreement could be reached.
